name: money-surfaces-visual
description: Redesign P5: Contracts, Finances, and Operations panels rendered with real state — a blasted plan (spend + fragments + logistics), one negotiated offer, one accepted contract, and a shift-policy change. Plan origin (5,5), not (10,10): see blast-workshop-french-visual.json's own note on the pre-existing (10,10)-seed-42 terrain-remesh crash this sidesteps. Setup split so the blast pipeline steps are individually role-marked and clicked for real (issue #479); the multi-offer contract targeting is real clicks scoped by data-contract-id (#513) after a setup tick establishes offers exist at all (see step descriptions).

steps.description: Staffed opening (#551): a driller with blasting + drill_rig licence, plus an unmanned drill_rig, are hired/purchased for free at game-open — #553's automatic drill dispatch needs both to ever land an ordered hole.

Contract offers refresh only every CONTRACT_REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks (events.ts) or via an explicit `contract list`; a fresh new_game seeds none (confirmed directly: `contract accept id:2` fails with "not found in available list" in both modes without this step). Advances to the first refresh boundary so contracts 1/2/3 genuinely exist before the accept/negotiate step below reaches for them by id. Confirmed via a real run: no event fires for seed 42 across ticks 1-20, and cash is unaffected (no employees/buildings/vehicles exist yet to incur payroll/upkeep/fuel).

steps.command: drill_plan grid origin:5,5 rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6
steps.description: Split out of the original bundled setup step (issue #479). This grid's spacing:3 already matches the placement strip's default (DEFAULT_SPACING_M, Drill.ts) — unlike blast-drill-plan-ui.json/blast-drill-plan-visual.json (Finding #4), no stepper clicks are needed for the click to reach the declared 2x2 pattern. #553: confirming the grid queues 4 drill_hole PendingActions and pushes 4 PlannedHoles into plannedDrillHoles — none drilled yet, so holeCount stays 0 right after confirm.
#553: drain the ordered plan — the staffed driller/drill_rig lands all 4 holes well inside this pad (sandbox-measured landing at tick 35 after this file's own tick 20 contract-refresh wait).
#554: drain the charge order(s) queued by the step above (charging is real work, not instant) before continuing.

expect.note: a fired blast clears the plan back to zero; confirmed against the real dump — cash does not change here (charge/blast spend is not reflected in the serialized cash field for this pipeline, unlike a building/vehicle purchase)

steps.description: #513 fix landed: offered-contract cards now carry `data-contract-id`, so negotiating one contract and accepting a different one specifically is a reliable, scoped click instead of only ever reaching "the first offer". Converted from three commands to real clicks: open the contracts panel, negotiate on a rubble_disposal card's own `[data-action="negotiate"]`, then accept a different (ore_sale) card's own `.bs-contract-accept`. #554-followup (issue #586 CI): the fixed ids (`data-contract-id="1"`/`"2"`, `contract accept id:2`) drifted out of the offer pool -- CONTRACT_REFRESH_INTERVAL=20 ticks (Contract.ts) keeps rotating ids out from under a fixed reference, and #554's real per-hole charging added a whole extra queue-drain wait (the `wait_until field:orderedChargeCount` step above) worth of additional elapsed ticks before this step ever runs, on top of the drift class already fixed the same way in core-loop-visual.json/economy-full-loop.json/safety-projection-visual.json. Direct trace at the point this step actually runs (tick 79, command mode) shows 8 offers including 2 rubble_disposal (ids 1, 7) and 1 ore_sale/sparkium (id 2, the original hardcoded target) among others -- retargeted by `type:` (ContractSelector, #597) instead: `type:rubble_disposal` for negotiate (any offer of that type; this file never cares which specific rubble contract, only that negotiating one and accepting a different one are two distinct real clicks) and `type:ore_sale` for accept (distinct type from the negotiate target, so the two clicks can never collide on the same card even if the exact id/material drifts). `command` also switched from the stale `id:2` to `type:ore_sale` so command mode and interaction mode target the same kind of contract. Timeouts widened (30s waitForSelector, 75s step budget) for the same real-time-vs-game-tick throughput reason as economy-full-loop.json's own contract-accept fix.
Contracts panel: storage strip, one active card, offered cards with the negotiate result inline on #1

expect.note: 'blocked' here is used for presence, not the usual guard-proof: a Deliver row only renders on an ACCEPTED contract's card (offered cards show Accept/Negotiate/Decline instead), so its presence proves id:2 actually got accepted. It's disabled (confirmed via a real interaction-mode run), since nothing has been hauled to storage yet to deliver — that's why 'blocked' (present, not reachable) is correct here rather than 'usable'.

steps.description: Finances panel: real balance/trend/runway, category bars from the blast spend, ledger — opened via the TopBar balance click, not a rail button

expect.note: toolbar panels are mutually exclusive — opening Finances via the TopBar balance click must hide Contracts

steps.description: Operations panel: logistics rows from the blast's fragments, empty ore-on-hand/incidents states, site policy card

expect.note: the Apply control the next step clicks must already be usable once this panel is open

steps.description: Operations panel: clicking a shift pill and Apply is a real, clickable interaction — pill highlight updates, note text changes, Apply dispatches set_policy
